330508.title: Dehmer–Kraus's extremal dendrimer entropy conjecture
330508.statement:
Let $D$ be a dendrimer on $n$ vertices with radius $r$ and progressive degree $p$. Let $\bar c_0,\bar c_1,\ldots,\bar c_r$ be a nonincreasing sequence of orbit weights, and let $I_{f^3}(D)$ be the corresponding entropy. The star has $r=1$ and $p=n-2$, while the path has $r=\lceil (n-1)/2\rceil$ and $p=1$.

**Dehmer–Kraus's conjecture.** For every sequence

$$
\bar c_0\geq \bar c_1\geq\cdots\geq\bar c_r,
$$

the star graph has the maximal value and the path graph has the minimal value of $I_{f^3}(D)$.

The conjecture was proposed from numerical experiments, with ideas toward a proof. It concerns the extremal entropy among dendrimers for all nonincreasing orbit-weight sequences.

330518.title: Pai et al.'s hypercube incidence coloring conjecture
330518.statement:
For an integer $n\geq 1$, let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube, with vertex set $\{0,1\}^n$ and edges between vertices differing in exactly one coordinate. Let $\chi_i(Q_n)$ denote its incidence chromatic number. **Pai et al.'s hypercube incidence coloring conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$ such that $n\neq 2^p-1$ for every integer $p\geq 1$, 
$$
\chi_i(Q_n)=n+2.
$$
 The conjecture was answered affirmatively in the source, so the asserted formula is known for all dimensions covered by its hypotheses.

332393.title: The bounded-colour-diameter covering conjecture for countable graphs
332393.statement:
For each integer $k\geq2$, there is a positive constant $C_k$. Given a $k$-colouring of a countably infinite graph $G$, let $\operatorname{diam}_{c}G[A]$ denote the diameter of the subgraph induced by $A$ in colour $c$. **The bounded-colour-diameter covering conjecture.** There exist vertex sets $A_1,A_2,\dots,A_{k-1}$ covering $G$ and colours $c_1,c_2,\dots,c_{k-1}\in[k]$ such that

$$
\operatorname{diam}_{c_i}G[A_i]\leq C_k\qquad\text{for all }i\in[k-1].
$$

The statement is posed among further questions and conjectures about higher-dimensional grids, and no resolution is supplied in the given text.

332603.title: Infinite graph extension of the tree decomposition conjecture
332603.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, and let a **$T$-decomposition** of a graph $G$ mean a partition of the edge-set of $G$ into subgraphs isomorphic to $T$. **Canonical infinite tree decomposition conjecture.** For every tree $T$, there exists a natural number $k_{\infty}(T)$ such that every $k_{\infty}(T)$-edge-connected infinite graph $G$ has a $T$-decomposition.

This is proposed as a canonical extension of the finite tree decomposition conjecture to infinite graphs. The source presents it as a conjectural direction; no resolution is given in the supplied text.

332860.title: Baudon–Bensmail–Przybyło–Woźniak conjecture on the irregular chromatic index
332860.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph that admits an edge-decomposition into locally irregular subgraphs; such a graph is called **decomposable**, and let $\chi'_{\rm irr}(G)$ be the least number of parts in such a decomposition.

**Baudon–Bensmail–Przybyło–Woźniak conjecture.** For every decomposable graph $G$,

$$
\chi'_{\rm irr}(G)\leq 3.
$$

The conjecture asserts a constant bound on the number of locally irregular subgraphs needed to decompose any graph for which such a decomposition exists. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

333133.title: Multiple list-colouring conjecture for planar graphs
333133.statement: Let $m$ be a positive integer. A graph is **$(k,m)$-choosable** if, whenever each vertex is assigned a list of at least $k$ colours, there is an $m$-fold colouring assigning each vertex $m$ colours from its list such that adjacent vertices receive disjoint colour sets. **Multiple list-colouring conjecture.** There is a constant integer $m$ such that every planar graph is $(5m-1,m)$-choosable. Thomassen's $5$-choosability theorem gives $(5m,m)$-choosability for every positive integer $m$, while the paper's lower bound shows that the exact threshold lies below or at $5m$; determining whether the upper bound can be improved is the motivating open problem.

333742.title: Discrete Fuglede conjecture for spectral sets
333742.statement:
Let $M$ be a positive integer and let $d4d0\subset\mathbb Z_M$ be a nonempty set. Call $d4d0$ a **discrete spectral set** if there is a set $d4d1\subset\mathbb Z_M$ with $|d4d1|=|d4d0|$ such that the associated Fourier orthogonality conditions hold for distinct elements of $d4d1$. Say that $d4d0$ **tiles** $d4d1_M$ by translations if there is $T\subset\mathbb Z_M$ with

$$
\mathbb Z_M=\bigsqcup_{t\in T}(\mathcal A+t)\bmod M.
$$

**Discrete Fuglede conjecture.** A set $d4d0\subset\mathbb Z_M$ is a discrete spectral set if and only if it tiles $d4d1_M$ by translations. This is a finite analogue of Fuglede's conjecture; the source reports numerical verification for all $M\leq20$.

333826.title: Bounded diameter arboricity plus-one conjecture
333826.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, let $\Upsilon(G)$ denote its arboricity, and let $\Upsilon_{bd}(\mathcal{G})$ denote the bounded diameter arboricity of a graph class $\mathcal{G}$. For $k\geq 1$, write $\mathcal{A}_k$ for the class of graphs with arboricity at most $k$.

**Bounded diameter arboricity plus-one conjecture.** The class $\mathcal{A}_k$ has bounded diameter arboricity $k+1$, that is,

$$
\Upsilon_{bd}(\mathcal{A}_k)=k+1.
$$

The conjecture asks whether allowing one more forest always suffices to partition the edges of every graph of arboricity at most $k$ into forests with uniformly bounded component diameters. The paper proves it for $k\in\{2,3\}$, while the general case remains open.

334118.title: Greatest-element conjecture for ribbons with fixed dimensions
334118.statement:
Consider the partial order on $G$-equivalence classes of skew shapes defined by $A\leq B$ when $a_{A,
u}\leq a_{B,
u}$ for every partition $
u$, equivalently when $G_B-G_A$ is $G$ positive. Ribbons with a fixed number of rows and columns form a connected component of this poset. **Greatest-element conjecture.** In addition to its least element, this set of ribbons has a greatest element. The source gives no proof or resolution of this assertion.

334119.title: Greatest-element conjecture for permutations of a ribbon partition
334119.statement:
Fix a partition $\lambda$, and consider the ribbons whose row lengths are a permutation of the parts of $\lambda$, ordered by $G$ positivity: $A\leq B$ when $a_{A,
u}\leq a_{B,
u}$ for every partition $
u$. **Permutation-class extremal-element conjecture.** The set of ribbons which are permutations of $\lambda$ has both a least element and a greatest element. The source presents this as a conjecture about the induced $G$-positivity poset and gives no resolution.

334560.title: Fair perfect matchings in partitions of K_{n,n}
334560.statement:
Let $K_{n,n}$ be the complete bipartite graph with edge set partitioned into $E_1,\ldots,E_m$. For a perfect matching $F$, write $|F\cap E_i|$ for the number of its edges in $E_i$. **Fair perfect matching conjecture.** For every $j\leqslant m$, there exists a perfect matching $F$ in $K_{n,n}$ such that

$$
|F\cap E_i|\geqslant \left\lfloor\frac{|E_i|}{n}\right\rfloor\quad(i\ne j),\qquad |F\cap E_j|\geqslant \left\lfloor\frac{|E_j|}{n}\right\rfloor-1.
$$

The result is proved in the paper for $m=2,3$; the general case is left open.

334570.title: The degree and leading-coefficient conjecture for equal-exponent subgroup-counting polynomials
334570.statement: Let $p$ be prime, let $m\ge 1$, and let $N(p^m,p^m,p^m,p^m)$ denote the polynomial counting subgroups of $(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})^4$. **Equal-exponent degree conjecture.** For every $m\ge 1$, the degree of $N(p^m,p^m,p^m,p^m)$ is $4m$ and its leading coefficient is $1$. This is one of the conjectures formulated in the paper and is reported as confirmed by the examples computed there; no general proof or disproof is given in the supplied text.

334722.title: The 2-connected chromatic polynomial ear conjecture
334722.statement:
Let $G$ be a 2-connected $k$-chromatic graph of order $n>k\geq 4$. An **ear** is a new path or cycle that overlaps an existing graph only in its two endpoints. **The 2-connected ear conjecture.** For all $x\geq k$,

$$
\pi(G,x)\leq \frac{(x)_{\downarrow k}\pi(C_{n-k+2},x)}{x(x-1)},
$$

with equality holding if $G$ arises by attaching an ear to $K_k$. This is presented as a strengthening suggested by computations on small graphs; its validity beyond the cases discussed in the paper remains open.

334795.title: The three-color homothetic-copy conjecture for convex sets
334795.statement: Let $D$ be a convex set in the plane, and call a scaled and translated copy of $D$ without rotation a **homothetic copy** of $D$. Let $S$ be a finite set of points. **The three-color homothetic-copy conjecture.** For every plane convex set $D$ there is an $m$ such that any finite set of points admits a $3$-coloring such that any homothetic copy of $D$ containing at least $m$ points contains two points with different colors. The disk case is stated to remain open, while the source proves the conjecture for convex polygons.

334947.title: Refinement conjecture for the secant degeneracy length of binary-form strata
334947.statement:
Let $\mu\vdash d$ be a partition, let $\bar\mu$ denote the associated standard stratum, and let $\ell_{\bar\mu}$ and $\ell_{\mu'}$ denote the corresponding secant degeneracy lengths. Write $\mu'\succeq\mu$ for the refinement partial order. **Refinement conjecture.** For every partition $\mu\vdash d$, there exists a partition $\mu'\succeq\mu$ such that

$$
\ell_{\bar\mu}=\ell_{\mu'}.
$$

The claim is based on extensive calculations and appears in the paper's final list of open problems; no resolution is supplied in the source.

334964.title: Akbari–Alipour's unbounded gap conjecture for Latin arrays
334964.statement:
Let $\ell(n)$ be the least positive integer such that $\ell(n)\geqslant n$ and every Latin array of order $n$ with at least $\ell(n)$ distinct symbols contains a transversal. **Akbari–Alipour's unbounded gap conjecture.** For every integer $c$, there exists a positive integer $n$ such that

$$
\ell(n)>n+c.
$$
 This conjecture asserts that the number of distinct symbols needed to force a transversal can exceed the order by arbitrarily large amounts. The source gives no resolution, so its status remains open.

337294.title: Balister–Győri–Schelp pairing conjecture for set-sequential trees
337294.statement:
Let $n\geq 2$, and let $v_1,\dots,v_{2^{n-1}}$ be nonzero vectors in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ satisfying

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{2^{n-1}}v_i=0.
$$

A **pairing partition** is a partition of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ into pairs $(p_i,q_i)$ indexed by $1\leq i\leq 2^{n-1}$. **Balister–Győri–Schelp pairing conjecture.** For every such choice of the $v_i$, there is a pairing partition such that

$$
v_i=p_i+q_i\qquad(1\leq i\leq 2^{n-1}).
$$

The conjecture is the combinatorial condition needed by the proposed construction that extends a set-sequential tree with $2^{n-1}$ vertices by adding $2^{n-1}$ pendant edges; its resolution determines whether that construction works for every admissible sequence of attachment labels.

337352.title: The diameter conjecture for powers-of-two Bell-type Riordan graphs
337352.statement:
Let $CG_{2^k}$ be the relevant io-decomposable Riordan graph of the Bell type, and let $\operatorname{diam}(G)$ denote graph diameter. **Diameter conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{diam}(CG_{2^k})=k
$$

and there are no io-decomposable Riordan graphs $G_{2^k}\not\cong CG_{2^k}$ of the Bell type satisfying

$$
\operatorname{diam}(G_{2^k})=k
$$

for all $k\geq 1$.

This conjecture is presented as a corrected direction after the preceding diameter conjecture was disproved. The supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.

337528.title: Blue path cover conjecture for the complete symmetric infinite digraph
337528.statement: Let $\vec{K}_{\mathbb{N}}$ be the complete symmetric digraph on the natural numbers, with each directed edge coloured red or blue. A **red directed path of length $r$** is a directed path consisting of $r$ edges. **Blue path cover conjecture.** For every integer $r\geq 1$, if a 2-colouring of $\vec{K}_{\mathbb{N}}$ contains no red directed path of length $r$, then the vertices of $\vec{K}_{\mathbb{N}}$ can be covered by at most $r$ vertex-disjoint blue directed paths. The preceding discussion establishes an almost-cover by at most $r$ blue paths, and notes that the claim is known when $r<4$; the general case remains open.

337577.title: Divisibility conjecture for matching and characteristic polynomials of hypertrees
337577.statement:
Let $H\sqsubseteq\mathcal{H}$ be $k$-trees, where $k\geq 3$. Write $\varphi(H)$ for the matching polynomial of $H$ and $\phi(\mathcal{H})$ for its adjacency characteristic polynomial.

**Divisibility conjecture.** If $H\sqsubseteq\mathcal{H}$ are $k$-trees for $k\geq 3$, then

$$
\varphi(H)\mid\phi(\mathcal{H}).
$$

In particular, if $H\sqsubseteq\mathcal{H}$, then

$$
\phi(H)\mid\phi(\mathcal{H}).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by computations for induced subgraphs of a specific 3-uniform hypertree, where each matching polynomial divides the corresponding characteristic polynomial. It asks whether this divisibility persists for all contained $k$-trees and, in particular, for their adjacency characteristic polynomials.
